q: An Automotive Technology II student writes a detailed summary of a transmission leak diagnosis for the service file, covering symptoms, tests and the repair. This is:
o: effective written communication throughout the course

o: one that states the symptom, tests performed, findings and parts replaced

o: avoid repeating a failed repair and spot patterns

o: diagnosing the major components of a powered vehicle

o: proper handling and disposal of environmentally hazardous materials

o: is toxic to animals and people

q: An oscilloscope shows a technician:

o: inspecting, removing and replacing shock absorbers and struts and inspecting mounts

o: stores a large amount of energy that can cause injury

o: comparing the rotational speed of each wheel

o: demonstrating knowledge of the steps to remove and replace TPMS sensors

o: wear in the bearing on the loaded (right) side

o: the causes and effects of shorts, opens and resistance problems in circuits

o: replacing an electrical connector and terminal end

o: maintaining or restoring electronic memory functions

o: inspecting and testing the switches, connectors and wires of the starter control circuit

o: checked to prevent slipping and premature wear

o: uneven braking force from a sticking caliper or hose

o: measuring brake pedal height, reserve distance, travel and free play

q: A technician learns that the emissions monitors must complete a drive cycle before a car can pass a state inspection. She is describing:
o: the importance of operating all OBD II monitors for repair verification

o: cylinder cranking and running compression tests

o: a blown head gasket between them

Air heard hissing from the tailpipe during a leakage test points to a:
